markets: Operations in the United States and other regions; supplies ingredients to personal care, home care and industrial customers.
rationale: B2B ingredients supplier with low consumer awareness; some personal care customers but limited F1 marketing logic.

name: AM Green Group
desc: Indian green energy developer building large-scale green hydrogen, ammonia and renewable energy projects.
markets: Projects based in India; export offtake to Europe is planned, but production is at an early stage.
rationale: Early-stage green fuels developer with a sustainability story; F1 net-zero narrative fits, but marketing budget is uncertain.

name: ATI
desc: Produces specialty materials and components, including titanium and nickel alloys, mainly for aerospace and defense customers.
markets: Sells to aerospace, defense and industrial customers mainly in the United States and Europe, plus Asia.
rationale: B2B alloy supplier with aerospace and technology strengths; F1 suits materials showcase but marketing culture is limited.
changed: Renamed from Allegheny Technologies to ATI

name: CABB
desc: Produces fine chemicals and agrochemical intermediates, including chloroacetic acid and its derivatives.
markets: German-headquartered producer selling intermediates to agrochemical and other industrial customers; sites and markets are not confirmed here.
rationale: Low-profile B2B intermediates maker with no consumer brand, so an F1 partnership makes little commercial sense.

name: Chemtrade Logistics
desc: Supplies industrial chemicals and services, including sulphuric acid and water treatment chemicals, mainly in North America.
markets: Plants and customers mainly in Canada and the United States, with limited operations elsewhere.
rationale: Industrial chemicals supplier with no consumer brand; regional focus makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Hoshine Silicon Industry
desc: Chinese chemical manufacturer producing industrial silicon metal and organosilicon products.
markets: Chinese producer with major operations in China; export sales are not confirmed from the available data.
rationale: Industrial materials producer with no consumer brand and mainly Chinese customers, so an F1 partnership makes little commercial sense.

name: Neo Performance Materials
desc: Supplies advanced industrial materials, focused on rare earth magnets and magnetic powders, from plants in Europe and Asia.
markets: Plants in Estonia, China and elsewhere supplying magnets and materials to customers in Europe, Asia and North America.
rationale: B2B rare earth supplier with an EV supply-chain story; F1 offers technology showcase but consumer reach is limited.

name: Novanta
desc: Makes photonics, vision and precision motion components and subsystems for medical and advanced industrial equipment makers.
markets: Sells components to medical and industrial equipment makers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B component supplier with a technology profile but little consumer brand; F1 gives modest showcase and hospitality value.

name: AXT Inc
desc: Produces compound semiconductor substrates such as gallium arsenide and indium phosphide, with manufacturing in China.
markets: Sells substrates to chip makers in Asia, North America and Europe, manufacturing mainly in China.
rationale: B2B substrate supplier with low brand profile; F1 technology link exists but marketing scale is small.

name: Bachem
desc: Manufactures peptides and oligonucleotides as active ingredients for pharmaceutical and biotech customers.
markets: Production sites in Switzerland and elsewhere supplying pharmaceutical and biotech customers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: B2B pharma ingredient maker with little consumer marketing; F1 hospitality has limited relevance.

name: Brenntag
desc: Distributes industrial and specialty chemicals and ingredients, connecting producers with customers in many industries.
markets: Distribution network across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and other regions with many thousands of customers.
rationale: Global B2B distributor with little consumer exposure; F1 hospitality could suit supplier and customer relationships.

name: CuspAI
desc: Applies artificial intelligence to materials discovery, offering a platform for finding new materials for industry.
markets: UK-based start-up; customers, partners and international plans are not confirmed from the available data.
rationale: Early-stage AI start-up with no consumer brand; technology showcase possible, but budget and awareness goals are limited.

name: Phoenix Tailings
desc: Produces rare earth metals and alloys using a lower-emission refining process.
markets: Operations in the United States; customers and international plans are not confirmed from the available data.
rationale: Early-stage rare earths producer with a clean-process story; limited budget makes an F1 deal unlikely.

name: Quaker Houghton
desc: Makes process fluids and chemical specialties, including metalworking fluids, for steel, automotive and industrial customers.
markets: Sells to steel, aluminium, automotive and industrial customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B fluids supplier to automotive and metals plants; F1 offers hospitality for industrial clients, but consumer reach is minimal.
changed: Renamed from Quaker Chemical to Quaker Houghton in 2020

name: Avient
desc: Makes specialty polymer materials, colorants and composites for packaging, consumer, healthcare and transportation customers.
markets: Sells to customers worldwide, with plants across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global materials supplier with automotive and consumer customers; F1 offers materials showcase and hospitality, though brand awareness is low.
changed: Formed from PolyOne, renamed Avient in 2020

name: AZZ
desc: Provides hot-dip galvanizing and coil coating services for steel and metal products.
markets: Plants in the United States and Canada serving construction, infrastructure and industrial customers.
rationale: Regional metal coating services provider with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Chandra Asri
desc: Indonesia's largest integrated petrochemical producer, making olefins, polyethylene, polypropylene and other polymers for industrial customers.
markets: Main operations in Indonesia; exports to other Asian markets are not confirmed here.
rationale: Industrial petrochemical producer with little consumer marketing; regional hospitality value is modest.

name: Eastman Chemical
desc: Produces specialty materials, additives, fibers and plastics, including recycled materials, for transportation, packaging and consumer markets.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe and Asia in automotive, packaging and consumer goods.
rationale: Global materials brand with automotive film and sustainability story; F1 offers materials showcase and hospitality.

name: Trinseo
desc: Produces specialty plastics, latex binders and synthetic rubber for automotive, packaging and consumer customers.
markets: Plants in the Americas, Europe and Asia serving automotive, packaging and construction customers.
rationale: B2B plastics supplier with automotive customers but financial pressure and low consumer profile; modest F1 fit.

name: Fabbrica Italiana Sintetici
desc: Italian maker of active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates and custom synthesis for generic and branded drug companies.
markets: Italian producer supplying drug makers worldwide; specific markets are not confirmed here.
rationale: B2B pharmaceutical ingredient maker with no consumer brand, so an F1 partnership makes little commercial sense.

name: Kraton
desc: Produces styrenic block copolymers and pine-based specialty chemicals for adhesives, tyres, coatings and consumer goods.
markets: Plants in the United States, Europe and Brazil supplying customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Materials supplier with tyre and consumer applications but no consumer brand; modest F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by DL Chemical in 2022

name: Outokumpu
desc: Produces stainless steel for construction, transport, appliances and industrial customers.
markets: Mills in Europe and the Americas supplying customers mainly in Europe and North America, with some Asian sales.
rationale: Industrial steel producer with a recycled-content story; F1 hospitality has some value, but there is little consumer marketing.

name: Spiber
desc: Japanese biotechnology company that makes Brewed Protein structural protein materials through microbial fermentation, sold to apparel brands.
markets: Based in Japan with a production plant in Thailand; apparel and fashion partners mainly in Japan.
rationale: Fashion-linked sustainable materials start-up; a technology showcase is possible, but scale and budget are small.

name: Boom Supersonic
desc: Developing the Overture supersonic passenger airliner, with airline customers placing pre-orders.
markets: Based in Colorado with a flight test programme; airline customers in the United States and Japan hold pre-orders.
rationale: Pre-revenue aircraft developer with strong technology brand; F1 speed narrative fits, but finances are limited.

name: Carpenter Technology
desc: Makes specialty alloys and stainless steels for aerospace, medical, transportation and energy customers.
markets: Sells to aerospace, medical and industrial customers mainly in North America, with sales in Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B alloy supplier with motorsport-adjacent materials expertise; limited consumer marketing, so modest F1 fit.

name: Maire
desc: Engineering and technology group building process plants and developing energy transition technologies for energy and chemicals customers.
markets: Projects and technology licensing for energy and chemicals clients across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Engineering contractor with a Middle East client base; F1 could provide B2B hospitality and sustainability positioning.
changed: Group rebranded from Maire Tecnimont to Maire

name: Odfjell Drilling
desc: Offshore drilling and well services contractor operating drilling rigs for oil and gas companies.
markets: Operates rigs and provides well services for oil companies in the North Sea, Australia and other regions.
rationale: B2B drilling contractor with a small marketing profile; client hospitality has some value but F1 fit is weak.
